source: Belfield, S. and Brown, C. (2010). Guidebook on Upland Crops in Cambodia: Corn (សៀវភៅណែនាំ ស្តីពីដំណាំតំបន់ខ្ពង់រាបនៅក្នុងប្រទេសកម្ពុជា៖ ដំណាំពោត). ACIAR Monograph 143, published by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in partnership with NSW Department of Primary Industries, the Cambodian Agricultural Research and Development Institute (CARDI), Murdoch University, University of Canberra, and MAFF, under ACIAR Project ASEM/2000/109. text:
A soil chemistry survey (Martin and Belfield 2007) sampled the topsoil (0-20 cm) of the main corn-growing soil groups in Battambang and Kampong Cham provinces, in both the February-March and July-August periods. Results (organic carbon %, total nitrogen %, pH, and nitrate-N in ppm):

- Kampong Cham, sandy/light-textured soil group: organic carbon 1.45%, total N 0.128%; Feb-Mar pH 5.5 / nitrate-N 28 ppm; Jul-Aug pH 5.0 / nitrate-N 10 ppm.
- Kampong Cham, Kampong Siem soil group: organic carbon 2.13%, total N 0.165%; Feb-Mar pH 5.7 / nitrate-N 20 ppm; Jul-Aug pH 5.4 / nitrate-N 12 ppm.
- Battambang, sandy/light-textured soil group: organic carbon 2.07%, total N 0.176%; Feb-Mar pH 5.8 / nitrate-N 20 ppm; Jul-Aug pH 5.5 / nitrate-N 38 ppm.
- Battambang, Kampong Siem soil group: organic carbon 2.56%, total N 0.181%; Feb-Mar pH 6.7 / nitrate-N 22 ppm; Jul-Aug pH 6.5 / nitrate-N 50 ppm.

These figures illustrate that Cambodia's main corn soils are generally acidic (pH in the 5-7 range) and relatively low in organic carbon and total nitrogen, with nitrate-N levels that shift noticeably between the dry and wet parts of the year -- important context for planning fertilizer programs.
